domain_restrictions: a, b, and r are integers.
The ordering restriction 0 <= a <= b is part of the hypotheses.
r is required to be nonnegative.
q is a formal indeterminate, not a numeric parameter.
n in the q-Pochhammer definition is a nonnegative integer.
j in the q-Pochhammer product is a positive integer.
d in the hypothesis ranges over all positive integers.
d in the conclusion ranges over the finite interval from 1 to r+b.
The q-Pochhammer value at n = 0 is defined to be 1.
The product over d from 1 to r+b is finite; if r+b = 0, the intended empty-product convention may be relevant.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For integer parameters a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, if the floor inequality holds for every positive integer d, then each explicitly defined exponent e_d is nonnegative for every d between 1 and r+b, and the ratio of q-Pochhammer symbols R_{a,b,r}(q) factors as a finite product of cyclotomic polynomials Phi_d(q) with those exponents. Therefore R_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial with integer coefficients.
quantifier_order: Choose integers a, b, r satisfying 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0.
Assume that for every positive integer d, the stated floor inequality holds.
For every integer d with 1 <= d <= r+b, define e_d by the given floor formula.
For every such d, conclude that e_d is nonnegative.
Conclude that R_{a,b,r}(q) equals the finite product over d from 1 to r+b of cyclotomic polynomials Phi_d(q) raised to e_d, and hence lies in the integer polynomial ring in q.

variables.name: q
variables.role: base variable for the q-Pochhammer symbols and cyclotomic polynomials

variables.name: n
variables.role: index in the definition of the q-Pochhammer symbol

variables.name: j
variables.role: product index in the definition of the q-Pochhammer symbol

variables.domain: positive integers; later restricted to 1 <= d <= r+b
variables.name: d
variables.role: divisor index in the hypothesis and in the cyclotomic factorization

variables.domain: integers indexed by d with 1 <= d <= r+b
variables.name: e_d
variables.role: cyclotomic exponent defined from floor functions

witness_dependencies: The exponent e_d depends explicitly on the parameters a, b, r and on the chosen index d.
There is no existential witness in the conclusion; the factorization is given explicitly by the displayed exponents.
The claim that R_{a,b,r}(q) is in the integer polynomial ring follows from the explicit nonnegative exponent factorization, not from choosing auxiliary objects.

statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, and set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b). Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then for every integer d with 1 <= d <= r+b, the integer e_d := floor((r+b)/d) + floor(a/d) - floor((r+a)/d) - floor(b/d) is nonnegative, and one has the cyclotomic factorization R_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{d=1}^{r+b} Phi_d(q)^(e_d), where Phi_d(q) is the d-th cyclotomic polynomial. In particular, R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q].
